thread:
Maya (oncall): Heads-up: we got a P0 from ACME on increased p95/p99 for text-gen in prod EU region. Started ~10:04 UTC. Customers seeing spikes ~2-3x baseline.

infra-monitor: alert: latency_p95 > 1200ms for /v1/generate (eu-west-2)

Maya (oncall): thanks. Repro steps from support below. Repro says single short prompt, sync call, 1-2s previously, now 5-8s.

Sara M.: pasted repro from customer: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"large-alpha","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}'``

Josh K.: grabbing traces. Querying span traces for traceid from logs...

Deploy Bot: rollout: model/large-alpha v3 -> v4 canary 10% at 09:50 UTC

Priya S.: could be canary perf regression. Any perf diff between v3 and v4?

Liam T.: preliminary: v4 increases kv-cache miss rate for short prompts due to tokenization change, adds ~30-40ms per request but shouldn't cause 3x. Also seeing queuing on batchers: active queue depth spiked.

Maya (oncall): action plan: 1) quick mitigations (rate limits/circuit breakers/region fallback) 2) deeper root-cause. Need playbook steps we can run asap.

Josh K.: Mitigations I'd run now (in order):
- flip canary -> rollback v4 to v3 (if canary is causing variance)
- enable circuit-breaker on route /v1/generate p99 threshold 2.0s (open for 60s)
- tighten per-API-key concurrency to 4 for affected customer (temp throttle)
- fallback routing: route eu-west-2 -> eu-west-1 if node saturation > 80%

Priya S.: Also consider temporary model fallback to quantized-smaller model: model/large-alpha-quant (same logits, lower latency) as emergency fallback.

Maya (oncall): good. Who can roll back canary? Josh?

Josh K.: on it. Rolling canary back now.

Deploy Bot: deploy event: rollback model/large-alpha v4 -> v3 at 10:08 UTC (triggered by Josh K.)

infra-monitor: event: queue_depth decreased after rollback, p95 improved from 1300ms -> 900ms but p99 still high at 1800ms

Liam T.: p99 tail not fixed. Hypothesis: downstream GPU contention on some hosts due to batching policy change in v4 config also applied cluster-wide. Need to reduce batch size and enforce per-host concurrency guard.

Priya S.: Can we activate a circuit-breaker that fails fast to smaller model? Example policy: if latency > 1.5s for 15s, route requests to large-alpha-quant for 60s and mark for audit.

Maya (oncall): yes. Create temporary routing rule. Liam, can you patch routing?

Liam T.: patching now. Rule:
```
if avg_latency(15s) > 1500ms:
  route(model=large-alpha-quant, region=eu-west-1)
  set circuit_breaker(open, duration=60s)
```
Applying...

infra-monitor: rule applied. Some traffic now hitting large-alpha-quant. Observed p95 -> 600ms, p99 -> 900ms for those flows.

Sara M.: contacted customer w/ update and temporary quota increase + explain fallback. Customer accepted temporary reroute to eu-west-1.

Josh K.: also adding a rate-limit tweak scoped to high token requests: reduce max tokens from 4096 -> 1024 for non-enterprise keys in eu region to reduce GPU long-running jobs.

Maya (oncall): logging quick reproducible command for SRE runbook (include trace headers):
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'X-Trace-Id: <trace-id>' \
  -d '{"model":"large-alpha","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```
Collect trace id from response headers and link to tracing UI: https://console.redwood/traces/<trace-id>

Priya S.: note for postmortem: include perf comparison between v3 and v4 at both 32 and 128 token loads, and batcher config diff. Also force-run synthetic load in canary env.

Liam T.: temporary mitigations in place. Next steps:
- revert any accidental batching config changes cluster-wide (investigate config rollout system)
- add a per-host circuit-breaker early-fail (50ms queue wait threshold)
- implement adaptive batching limit for short-seq workloads

Josh K.: I'll open an incident ticket with runbook steps I executed + commands + screenshots.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. Quick checklist for shift handover:
- keep circuit-breaker enabled until next deploy window
- monitor p95/p99 for next 6 hours and alert if > baseline*1.5
- SRE owner: Liam, Postmortem owner: Priya, Customer comms: Sara

Sara M.: customer follow-up scheduled 11:00 UTC. Sending interim note now. :white_check_mark:

infra-monitor: metric: p95 normalized now 580ms, p99 820ms (eu-west-2 overall)

Maya (oncall): closing immediate oncall thread; will convert to incident doc. Leave this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
